cells.remarks: SAUNDATTI, PARASGAD TALUK, BELGAUM DISTRICT (B. K. No. 58 of 1935-36) On a slab set up in the Basti-guḍi Krishṇa II — A. D. 875-76 The inscription in Sanskrit and Kannada language is dated in Śaka 797, Manmatha, but is engraved in characters of about the 11th or 12th century A. D. The Śaka and the cyclic year correspond to A. D. 875-76. It records a grant of eighteen nivartanas of land by Mahāsāmanta Prithvirāma, the son Mērada, to a Jinēndra-bhavana got built by himself. The donee is stated to be the disciple of Indrakīrtisvāmin who in turn was the disciple of Guṇakīrti-munīśvara. The latter again was the disciple of Muḷḷabhaṭṭa of Mailāpatīrtha and Kārēyagaṇa. Lines 1 to 4 record a later grant, made by Kanna, of six nivartanas of land in the sīvaṭa Mulgunda in Sugandhavartti-12. Lines 18-19 state that the grant made by Prithvīrāma was renewed by Kārttavirya and (his wife) Bhāgalāmbikā on the occasion of a solar eclipse. The donors of all the grants are of the Raṭṭa family, Mērada being the first member. Text1

cells.remarks: —A. D. 980 The record is dated Śaka 902, Vikrama, Paushya, śu. 10, Thursday, Uttarāyaṇa- Saṅkrānti. The Saṅkrānti occurred on Thursday, December 23, A. D. 980. The tithi was, however, śu. 14 on that day and not śu. 10 as stated in the record. The inscription registers the grant of 150 mattars of land by the Raṭṭa chief Śāntivarmarasa to the Jaina monastery (basadi) caused to be constructed by him at Sugandhavarti (i. e., modern Saundatti). The genealogy of this chief is given. The gift was entrusted to Bāhubali-bhaṭṭāraka. It also records another gift of 150 mattars of land by the chief’s mother Nijiyabbarasi to the same monastery. The record is published in JBBRAS. Vol. X, p. 204. 1. Continuation is worn out.

text.remarks:
—A. D. 980

The record is dated Śaka 902, Vikrama, Paushya, śu. 10, Thursday, Uttarāyaṇa-
Saṅkrānti. The Saṅkrānti occurred on Thursday, December 23, A. D. 980. The tithi
was, however, śu. 14 on that day and not śu. 10 as stated in the record.

The inscription registers the grant of 150 mattars of land by the Raṭṭa chief
Śāntivarmarasa to the Jaina monastery (basadi) caused to be constructed by him at
Sugandhavarti (i. e., modern Saundatti). The genealogy of this chief is given. The
gift was entrusted to Bāhubali-bhaṭṭāraka. It also records another gift of 150 mattars
of land by the chief’s mother Nijiyabbarasi to the same monastery.

The record is published in JBBRAS. Vol. X, p. 204.

cells.remarks: —A. D. 1015 This is dated Śaka 936, Ānanda, Phālguṇa, Amāvāsya, Sunday, Saṅkrānti, corres- ponding to A. D. 1015, February 20, Sunday, f. d. t. 56. The Mīna saṅkrānti occurred on the following day. The record gives a genealogical account of the Chālukya dynasty in the begin- ning commencing from Raṇarāga, son of Jayasiṁha I, and ending with Vasudhai- kamalla Ayyaṇadēva. It registers a gift of 60 mattars of land, three gardens, one oil-mill and three shops, by Mahāsāmanta Dēvaṇarasa described as the brother of the king, to god Nagarēśvara. Moraḍiya Chāmuṇḍayya, the Sēnabōva, wrote the record. It mentions Chandraśēkharāchārya of the Nagarēśvara temple and also certain other individuals.

It records that while the king was ruling from Ētagiri, and his son Mahāsāmanta Dāsarasa was governing the eighteen agrahāras including Rūvige, situated in Tarddavāḍi-nāḍu, Mahāsāmanta Dhanasaṅgrahayyarasa of the Seḷara family made a gift of land to God Nagarēśvara of Āneya-Rūvige, for worship and offerings as also for the maintenance of the ascetics of the place. The gift was entrusted to Bāḷachandrapaṇḍita. The king is stated to have been ruling from his capital (neleviḍu) Ētagiri.

cells.dynasty: Bhuvanaikamalla (Sōmēśvara II) · Sōmēśvara II
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1069 This badly damaged record is dated Śaka 991, Kīlaka, Amāvāsyā, Sunday, Dakshiṇāyana [saṁkrānti]. This date is irregular. The cyclic year corresponding to the given Śaka year was Saumya and not Kilaka. The intended date seems to be A. D. 1069, June 21 when the tithi was amāvāsyā and the week-day was Sunday. The Saṁkrānti, however, occurred three days later. The inscription records the gift of certain money incomes made by Mādhavayya Nāyaka with the permission of the king for the benefit of the temple of Nakharēśvara at Rūvige when Pāyyarasa was governing Tardavāḍi division. The inscription also refers to another gift of oil made by the Fifty Telliga tenants for a lamp in the temple of Kēdārēśvara of the place (i. e., Rūvige) in the year Śaka 967, Pārtthiva, Pushya śu. 5, Sunday Uttarāyaṇa-Saṁkrānti. This date corresponds to A. D. 1045, December 15, Sunday, f. d. t. 64. There was no Saṁkrānti on this date. It appears that this gift was revived as in the case of No. 45 below.

cells.place: Slab built into the wall of the store-room in the Jaina basadi
cells.dynasty: Bhuvanaikamalla (Sōmēśvara II) · Sōmēśvara II
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1072 This record is dated Śaka 994, Paushya, śu. 11, Monday, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṁkrānti corresponding regularly to A. D. 1072, December 24. The inscription records the revival of the endowment of the village Guḍigēre, formerly made by Kumkumamahādēvi, the younger sister of the Chālukya king Vijayāditya, to Ānesejjeya-basadi which was caused to be constructed by her a Puligere. The gift is stated to have been made by queen Kamchalamahādēvi who was governing from the headquarters at Muḷugunda and others in the presence of the king, with the consent of Bhāskara-bhaṭṭōpādhyāya on the occasion of his victorious return from the northern expedition. It is also stated that Mahāpradhāna Daṇḍa- nāyaka Rudrabhaṭṭōpādhyāya was administering Guḍigēre and Daṇḍanāyaka Īśvara- bhaṭṭa was in charge of all the departments. The donee was Nandi-paṇḍitadēva.

cells.place: Slab set up near the temple of Sōmēśvara
cells.dynasty: Bhuvanaikamalla (Sōmēśvara II) · Sōmēśvara II
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1076 (?) The record is dated Śaka 998, Rākshasa, Pushya, Amāvāsya, Sunday, Hasta nakshatra, Uttarāyaṇa-saṃkrānti. The details of this date are irregular. The Śaka year 998 corresponded to the Cyclic year Anala when the said saṃkrānti occurred on Saturday, the tithi being ba. 11 of the month Pushya and the nakshatra Viśākhā. In the cyclic year Rākshasa the saṃkrānti occurred on Friday the tithi being śu. 15 and the nakshatra Punarvasu. The intended date might be 1076 A.D., December 24, Saturday. The inscription registers the gift of the village Puḷḷavaḷa situated to the south of the river Varadā in Bāsavura-140, a sub-division of Banavāsi-12,000, to God Svayambhū Sōmēśvara of Kalkēre, for worship and offerings to the deity and for feeding the ascetics, etc., by Bhuvanaikamalla-Vira-Noḷamba who was governing Noḷambavāḍi, Pānumgaḷḷu-nāḍu and Banavāsidēśa. The gift was made, in conjunction with his wife Māḷaladēvi, at the request of Perggaḍe Divākara and was entrusted to Dēvasinga Jīya. The king was at that time camping at Baṅkāpura. The record contains an eulogy of the donor and his wife.

cells.remarks: —A. D. 1077 The record is dated Chālukya-Vikrama year 2, Piṁgala, Pushya, śu. 7, Sunday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti, corresponding to A. D. 1077, December 24. The tithi, however, was śu. 2 and not śu. 7. The inscription records gifts of land for the benefit of the temple of Chaṇḍēśvara at Kumbiṭṭage, by Mahāsāmanta Siṁgarasa of Siyaḷāra family and Udāyādityarasa. It also records gifts of land, garden and oil to the same temple and also to the temple of Vināyaka and Ādityadēva by Kētaladēvi, queen of Tribhuvanamalladēva. The latter is said to have been ruling from his camping place at Poṇuguppe.

cells.remarks: —A. D. 1077-78 This record, written in Sanskrit and Kannada languages, is dated Śaka 969 (in words), Chālukya-Vikrama year 2, Piṁgala, Āshāḍha śu. 12, Wednesday corresponding regularly to A. D. 1077 July 5. There is a second date in the record the details of which are Śaka 1000, Kālayukta, Madhumāsa (Chaitra) Amāvāsya, Sunday. This corresponds to A. D. 1078, April 14. Saturday, on which day the tithi ended at 90. This inscription records the death of Śrīnandi-Paṇḍitadēva of Sūrastra-gaṇa by the rite of Sallēkhanā observed for one month at Anesejjeya-basadi at Purikara- nagara. It also records the death on the second date of Bhāskaranandi-Paṇḍita who is said to have been the elder brother of the former.

cells.location: SAUNDATTI, PARASAGAD TALUK, BELGAUM DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab set up in the Basti-gudi
cells.dynasty: Tribhuvanamalla (Vikramāditya VI) · Vikramāditya VI
cells.remarks: —A.D. 1098 (?) The record is dated Vira-Vikrama, i.e., Chālukya-Vikrama year 21, Dhātu, Pushya ba. 13, Sunday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti. The details given are irregular. The tithi corresponds to January 14, Wednesday, A.D. 1097. But in the next year, i.e. A.D. 1098, the tithi corresponds to January 3, when the weekday was Sunday. In neither case did the said Saṁkrānti occur. The latter date, viz., A.D. 1098, January 3 might be the intended date. The inscription records a gift, by the king, of land in Kāreyabāgu village to the temple of Jinēndra built by Kālasēna of the Raṭṭa family. It further records another gift of land by the Raṭṭa chief Sēna II to the same temple. It also refers to a gift of land made by the Raṭṭa chief Kannakaira II to his guru Kanakaprabhasiddhāntadēva. Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kārtavīrya is mentioned as the feudatory of the king. Published in JBBRAS, Vol. X, pp. 195-98.

cells.remarks: —A. D. 1109 This record is dated Chālukya-Vikrama year 34, Virōdhin, Mārggaśira, Puṇṇame, Monday, lunar eclipse, Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti. The details are irregular. The saṁkrānti occurred on Saturday, December 25, A. D. 1109, when the tithi was Puṣhya, śu. 2. The eclipse occurred on November 9, Tuesday when the tithi was Kārttika puṇṇame. The intended date might be A. D. 1109, November 8, Monday, f.d.t., 53. The inscription records a remission of taxes on the land (aruvaṇa) of the temple of Svayambhudēva at Khēḍa in the One Thousand division, by Lakshmīdhara- Bhaṭṭōpādhyāya, who was the preceptor of Yuvarāja Mallikārjunadēva, the eldest son of the king, who was then governing over the Tarddavāḍi- 1000 division. It further registers gifts of money income, taxes, etc., to the same temple by Mahāpradhāna, Permāḍiyarasa, Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Gōvaṇarasa of the Śilāra family whose genealogy also is given and by the Five Hundred Svāmis of Ayyāvoḷe and the Eight nāḍus.

cells.remarks: (Undated) This undated inscription is in Kannada and Sanskrit languages. cells.remarks: —A. D. 1140 This record is dated the 2nd regnal year, Siddhārthi, Pushya, Pauṛṇamāsyā, Sunday, Lunar eclipse, Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti. The date is irregular. The tithi corresponds to A.D. 1140, January 6, Saturday, and the saṁkrānti occurred on December 25 of the previous year, the weekday being Monday. The said eclipse did not occur on either of the days. The inscription, which is badly effaced, because of a thick coat of oil, records a gift of land, etc., made by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Sōvidēvarasa of the Seḷara family who was the manneya of Eḷamēla-nāḍu, at the instance of Perggaḍe Dāvarāja to the temple of Mūlasthāna Mallikārjunadēva built by the latter at Nāvidige in Eḷamēla-nāḍu-30. It gives a genealogical account of both these persons.

cells.location: SĀMSI, KUNDGOL TALUK, DHARWAR DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab lying near the house of Gurubassappa Kumbi
cells.dynasty: Jagadēkamalla II · Jagadēkamalla II
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1144 (?) This damaged record is dated in the regnal year of the king which is lost. The extant details of the date are Puṣya, Amāvāsyā, Monday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti, solar eclipse. During the reign of this king, the eclipse occurred on the said tithi, in A. D. 1144, December 22, which might be the probable date of this record. The weekday was, however, Tuesday. The inscription contains a second date, the only available details of which are Āṣāḍha, Amāvāsyā. The inscription seems to record a gift of land, house-sites, and shop to god Gavaṛēśvaradēva of the agrahāra of Savasi (also referred to as Tapasi-grāma) by the Four-Hundred Mahājanas who are praised in the beginning. It also records a gift of income from certain taxes by the Five-Hundred Svāmis of Ayyāvoḷe and the One Thousand Tambuligas to the same deity, made over to Īśānaśakti-paṇḍita, an ācārya of the Kāḷāmukha sect. The record which contains an eulogy of these svāmis seems to register another gift on the second date. But the details are all lost.

cells.remarks: —A. D. 1146 This record is dated in the king's regnal year 9, Akshaya, Puṣya, śu. 6, Monday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti. The date is irregular. The given tithi corresponds to A. D. 1146, December 10, Tuesday, but the saṅkrānti occurred on December 25, Wednesday. The inscription registers a gift of land, garden, oil-mill, shop, house-site and income from herijuṅka to the temple of Svayambhu-Rāmēśvara, built at Eraṅgal by the three brothers, Kēsirāja, Dāsiṇarasa and Viṭṭarasa. D. 1147 The record is dated in the king's regnal year 10, Prabhava, Āshāḍha śu, 12 Thursday, Dakshiṇāyana-saṅkramaṇa. śu. 12 seems to be a mistake for ba. 12 because the said saṅkramaṇa occurred on the latter day. Then the date of the record would regularly correspond to Thursday, 26th June, A. D. 1147. The inscription registers certain gifts of lands in Kunduravaḷḷi and Huligere made by Daṇḍanāyaka Mēcharasa when Daṇḍanāyaka Kēsimayya was governing Belvola-300, Huligere-300, Halasige-12,000 and Hānungal-500 and when Jayakēśi- dēva of the Maṇala family was the manneyam of Huligere-nāḍu. The record was composed by Karṇāṭasukavi Mukhya-paṇḍita and engraved by Chāvōja, the eldest son of Jinnōja of Puligere. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XVI, p. 44.

cells.dynasty: Permāḍi · Permāḍi
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1129 This record is dated in the king's regnal year 12, Saumya, Chaitra ba, 13, Monday, Solar eclipse. The date is irregular. The cyclic year Saumya which occurred during the reign of Permāḍi coincided with A. D. 1129 and the solar eclipse in Chaitra of that year occurred on Saturday, April 20. The inscription registers a grant of land made by Saṅkara-bhaṭṭōpādhyāya, the son of Chaṅgadēva-bhaṭṭōpādhyāya, who had obtained the gift land. The latter was the prabhu of Taddalabāge. The grant was made for the worship and offerings of God Sōmanātha at Taddalabāge. Grants of flower-garden, oil-mill, land and money, made by the sthānas and baṇañjigas are also recorded.

cells.remarks: —A. D. 1161 This record is dated Śaka 1083, 6th year of the king Bijjala, Visha, Āśvija Pūrṇimā, Monday, lunar eclipse. These details are not regular. The tithi given corresponds to A. D. 1161, October 6, which was Friday. There was an eclipse on that day. The inscription refers itself to the reign of Bijjala. It gives the genealogy of the Western Chālukya king Nūrmaḍi Taila (i. e., Taila III). Then follows an eulogistic account of Bijjala. It further states that while Vēsuva-nāyaka and four other karaṇas were administering Huligere-300, Dēvarāśi-paṇḍita, the āchārya of God Rāmaidēva and a disciple of Amṛtarāśi-paṇḍita, purchased some land from Raṭṭagavuṇḍa of Beḷuvana-grāma and granted the same for the worship of Muttina- keyya Indrēśvara. The village Beḷuvana is stated to have belonged to the temple of Rāmaiyadēva. 1. The continuation is very badly damaged.

cells.remarks: BHŪYĀR, INDI TALUK, BIJAPUR DISTRICT Broken slab near the ruined Mallikārjuna temple on the bank of the Bhīmarathī river Tribhuvanamalladēva (Bijjala)—A.D. 1162 This record is dated in the king's regnal year 7, Chitrabhānu, Vaiśākha, Amāvāsya, Monday. The details of the date correspond to A.D. 1162, May 16, which was a Wednesday and not Monday. 1. From this point onwards upto the end, the record is engraved in different characters. The inscription states that Mahāpradhāna, Daṇḍanāyaka Lakshmidēva who was governing Mūvattārum-bāḍa, visited Buyyāra for the purpose of taking bath in the river there and made a grant of land, jointly with the four karaṇas and others, headed by his perggaḍe Nāyaṇa-nāyaka, to Basavayya, the servant of Śivayōgi Sātayya of Neluvige for the benefit of the latter. A further gift to the temple of Abhinava-Mallikārjuna at Buyyāra, in the year Sarvadhāri during the reign of Rāyamurāri Sōvidēva, by Kopparasa, an officer of Mailēya-Nāyaka, Chikka-Chaṇḍarasa and others, is recorded at the end of the inscription.

cells.location: BĀLAMBĪḌ, HANGAL TALUK, DHARWAR DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab set up in the temple called Boḷadēv-guḍi
cells.dynasty: Bijjala · Bijjala
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1165 This record is dated the cyclic year Pārthiva, Kārtika, śu. Monday, Saṃkramaṇa Neither the Śaka nor the regnal year of the king is given. The tithi also is omitted. The cyclic year Pārthiva which occurred during the reign of Bijjala coincided with A. D. 1165 and the Śukla-paksha of Kārtika fell in October. In that paksha occurred two Mondays, one on the 11th and the other on the 18th of October. There was no Saṃkramaṇa on either of the days. In the absence of the tithi it is not possible to determine as to which of the two Mondays was intended. The inscription records a grant of land made by Kēśava-daṇḍanāyaka, the officer in charge of taxes (suṅkādhikāri) for the benefit of the temple of God Brahmēśvaradēva, attached to that of the God Chikēśvaradēva of Baḷḷarabiḍu. The grant was made in the presence of the karaṇas, headed by Siddhughi- daṇḍanāyaka, Hariharagāvuṇḍa, heggaḍe Biraṇa and others and was entrusted to Vimalaśaktidēva, the āchārya of the temple. The conquests of Bijjala are enumerated and the genealogy of Kēśava-daṇḍanāyaka is given.

cells.dynasty: Sōvidēva · Sōvidēva
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1170 This record is dated in the cyclic year Vikṛita, Jyēṣṭha, Amāvāsyā, Monday. The king's regnal year is not given but the cyclic year Vikṛita which fell in the reign of Sōvidēva, coincided with A. D. 1170. In this year, the details of the date correspond regularly to Monday, June 15, f.d.t. ·10. The inscription records a gift of land to Dugga-jīya made by Daṇḍanāyaka Basavarasa, an officer of Mailaya-nāyaka, his brother Kopparasa, Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vārarasa, the prabhu and gāvuṇḍas of Khēḍa, etc., out of the gift of 325 mattars of land which had been (formerly) made by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kailāsarasa, a subordinate of Subhatuṅgadēva to the temple of Kailāsadēva at Khēḍa, the rājadhāni of the Thirty- six-village (division) included in Tarddavāḍi-nāḍu. It also registers the gift of an oil-mill to the same temple, by Daṇḍanāyaka Basavarasa and refers to a previous gift, apparently to the same temple, made by Babbagāvuṇḍa and Lakshmādēvi on the occasion of a solar eclipse.

text.remarks:
—A. D. 1170
This record is dated in the cyclic year Vikṛita, Jyēṣṭha, Amāvāsyā, Monday.
The king's regnal year is not given but the cyclic year Vikṛita which fell in the reign
of Sōvidēva, coincided with A. D. 1170. In this year, the details of the date
correspond regularly to Monday, June 15, f.d.t. ·10.
The inscription records a gift of land to Dugga-jīya made by Daṇḍanāyaka
Basavarasa, an officer of Mailaya-nāyaka, his brother Kopparasa, Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara
Vārarasa, the prabhu and gāvuṇḍas of Khēḍa, etc., out of the gift of 325 mattars of
land which had been (formerly) made by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kailāsarasa, a subordinate
of Subhatuṅgadēva to the temple of Kailāsadēva at Khēḍa, the rājadhāni of the Thirty-
six-village (division) included in Tarddavāḍi-nāḍu. It also registers the gift of an
oil-mill to the same temple, by Daṇḍanāyaka Basavarasa and refers to a previous
gift, apparently to the same temple, made by Babbagāvuṇḍa and Lakshmādēvi on the
occasion of a solar eclipse.Read more (1 KB)

cells.remarks: BHŪYĀR, INDI TALUK, BIJAPUR DISTRICT Broken slab near the ruined Mallikārjuna temple on the bank of the Bhīmarathi river Sōvidēva—(A. D. 1172) This record is dated in the king's regnal year 4, Khara, Phālguna, Amāvāsye, Monday. The details of the date correspond to A. D. 1172, February 25, which was Friday and not Monday as stated in the record. The inscription registers a gift of land for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple of god Kūḍaladēva, by Dhāyya, Māya-sāhaṇi, Rēchagāvuṇḍa and others.

The king is stated to have been ruling from Seleyahaḷḷi. 46 [ನೆಂ] ದಣ್ಣನಾಯಕಂ ಕುಮಾರ ಬಮ್ಮಿ ದೇವರೆಸರ್ ಕಂದು ಹ್ರಷ್ಟ ಪುಷ್ಟರಾಗಿ ಈ ಸ್ಥಳದೋರೇನಂ ಮಾಡಿದೋದಮ– 47 ಕ್ಷಯಫಲವೆಂಬುದಂ ಧರ್ಮಶಾಸ್ತ್ರಂಗಳಂ ತಿಳಿದು ಈ ದೇವರ್ನಿನಿಯೋಗಕ್ಕೆ ತಮ್ಮ ಹೆಸರ ಧಮ್ಮF ವಾಗಿ ನ– 48 ದೇವನ್ನಾಗಿ ಭೂಮಿಯಂ ಪರಿಕಲ್ಪಿಸಿ ಕುಡಪೇಳ್ದೆಂದು ವೀರವೆನೆ ಹಿಡಿದ ಧಮ್ಮFಮನೆ ಬಿಡುವಂ ತ್ಯಾಗಕ್ಕೆ ಕಲ್ಪ– 49 ವೃಕ್ಷವೆನಿಸಿದ * ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ಹಾ ಮಂಡಳೇಶ್ವರಂ ಎಳಮೇಲ ಸಿಂಗಿದೇವರೆಸನುಂ ತಾನುಂ ಏಕಭಾವದಿಂ ಸುಮನಸ್ಸರಾ– 50 ಗಿ ಶಕನೃಪಾಬ್ದಂ ೧೧೯ಳನೆಯ ನಂದನಸಂವತ್ಸರದ ಪುಷ್ಯ ಸುದ್ಧ ಲ ಸೋಮವಾರ ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣ ಸಂಕ್ರಾಂತಿ ವ್ಯತೀಪಾ– 51 ತಂ ಕೂಡಿದಲ್ಲ ಕಡಲೆವಾಡದ ಶ್ರೀ ಸ್ವಯಂಭುಸೋಮನಾಥದೇವಗೆ೯ ಮುನ್ನ ಕನಪಯ್ಯನಾಯ ಕನುಂ 52 ಸಿಂಗಿದೇವರೆಸಂಗೆ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಭೂಮಿಯೊಳಗಾಗಿ ಮೂಡರಾ ದೇವವಳ್ಳ ಸೆಂದೇವಾಡದ ಪಡುಣಾ ನೀಮೆ ಮೂಡ– 53 ಲಾಗಿ ತೆಂಕಲು ಕುಮಸೆಯ ಪ್ರಭುಮಾನ್ಯಂ ಮೇರೆ ಪಡುವಲು ದೇವಣಗಾವೆಯ ನೀಮೆ ಬಡಗಲಾ ನೀಮೆಯ 54 ಹಿಟ್ಟನೆತ್ತು ಗುಟ್ಟ ಕಡಲೆವಾಡದ ಪೂರ್ವ್ವಾದ ಚತುಃಸೀಮಾಪಾಟದೊಳಗೆ ನಿಧಿನಿಧಾನನಿಕ್ಷೇಪತರು ಪಥ– 55 ಮಾಲಾಏಕ್ಷಜಲಪಾಷಾಣಸಹಿತ ತ್ರಿಭೋಗಾಧ್ಯನ್ರವಾದಿಯಾಗಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಸ್ಥಳವಿತ್ತಿಯುಕ್ತ– 56 ತ್ರಿಯಂ ದೇವರ್ನಿನಿಯೋಗವೆನ್ನೆಂದಡೆ ತ್ರಿಕಾರಾಚ್ಯFನಾರಂಕಾರ ಮಹಾನ್ವೇದ್ಯಕ್ಮಂ ಕಪ್ಪರ್ನರ 57 ತಾಂಬೂಳಕುಂಕುಮಚಂದನಾನುಲೇಪನಕ್ಮಂ ಗೀತವಾದ್ಯನೃತ್ಯಕ್ಮಂ ಚೈತ್ರಪವಿತ್ರಾರೋಪಣಕ್ಮಂ ಬಂದ– 58 ತ್ಸುಚತಜೇಣ್ಣ Fದಾರ್ನರ ಸೋತೆಸುಣು ಮಾಟಕೂಟಕ್ಮಂ ತಪೋದನರತನತಾ (ಜ್ಞಾ) ದನಕೃವಾ ಚಂದ್ರಾಕ್ಕFಸ್ಥಾಯಿ– 59 ಯಾಗಿ ಯಮ ನಿಯಮಾಸನಪ್ರಾಣಾಯಾಮಪ್ರತ್ಯಾಹಾರಧ್ಯಾನಧಾರಣಮೋನಾನುಷ್ಠಾ[ನ] ಜಪನಮಾಧಿಶೀಲಗುಣಸಂಪನ್ರರುಂ ವಿಬುಧಜನಮೋತ್ಸಿತ್ಥಫಲಸಮುತ್ಪನ್ನರುಂ ದೀನಾನಾಥಜತರ ರದಾ– 61 ವಫಾವಕನಿವಾರಣರುಂ ದುರಿತಮಡಗನಿವಾರಣರುಂ ನಿಜಸಮಯತರಣಯ್ತು ರಕ್ಷದಕ್ಷರುಂ ಅನ್ನ[ನ]– 62 ವರತಸುಭಿಕ್ಷರುಂ ಪಣ್ಣಿ ತಚೂಡಾಮಣಿಯುಂ ನಿಷ್ಪ ಜನಚಿನ್ಮಾಮಣಿಯುಂ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ನಾಮಾವಳೀ ವಿರಾಜಿತ– 63 ರುಮಪ್ಪ ಶ್ರೀಮದಲ್ಲಾಚಾರ್ಯ್ಕರು ಸೋವರಾಸಿಪಣ್ಣ ತದೇವಗೆ೯ ದಾರಾಪೂರ್ವಕಂ ಮಾಡಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟರು (0) 64 ಗೋಚಮ್ಮFಮಾತ್ರಭೂಮಿಯ ಧೂಚಕ್ರದೊಳತ್ತ ವಗ್ಗೆ ಸ್ವಗ್ಗ Fಫಲಂ ತಾನಾ ಚಮ್ಮF ಮಾರಿದಂ– 65 ದಂದಿನಾ ಚಮ್ಮFನ್ಸರದ ನಸಿಯ ಬೇಗ್ಗ ಳ ಪವನ || ವರೆವಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಕಡಿತಂ ಧ[ರ್ರೆ] ಬಳಪಂ ಹಿಮಗಿರೆಂದ್ರವಾದೊಡ– 66 ವೇನುಂ ನಿರುತಂ ಲೆಕ್ಕನೆಣ이ುಮ ಪರಮದ ಮುಂದೊಮ್ಮೆ ಮಾಲ್ವ ಭೋಗದ ಫಲಮಂ || ಇದ ರಕ್ಷಿಪಂಗೆ ಸಾಶ್ವತ ಪದವಿಗ– 67 ಲದಿಗೋಳು ವಿದುಟೊಳನೆಯಂ ಮಾಡುವಂಗೊದವಿ ದಾರವನರದ ಪುಳ್ಳ ಕೊಳದ್ದಿ ಕ್ಯು ಕ ಲ್ಪಕೋಟಿ ಸ– 68 ಹಸ್ರಂ || © ಶ್ರೀಮದಲ್ಲಾಚಾರ್ಯ್ಕರು ಸೋವರಾಸಿಪಣ್ಣ ತದೇವರು ತಮ್ಮ ಪುತ್ರ ಶ್ರೀ ಸೋಮ ನಾಥದೇವ– 69 ಪಾದಾರಾಧಕಂ ಸರಸ್ವತೀದೇವೀಲಬ್ಧಪ್ರಸಾದಂ ಪ್ರಾsನಾದಮಾಟಕೂಟಪ್ರವೀಣನಪ್ಪ 70 ಸೂತ್ರಧಾರಿ ಸಂಗೋಜಂಗೆಯಲ್ಲದು ದನದವಂ ಕೆಯ್ಯನಿಪ್ಪು ತು ಕಯ್ಯು ನಿವೇಷನವಿಷ್ಮ[ತು]

cells.location: KAḌALĒVĀḌ, SINDGI TALUK, BIJAPUR DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab set up in the temple of Śivaliṅga
cells.dynasty: Sōvidēva · Sōvidēva
cells.remarks: — A. D. 1176 This record is dated Śaka 1097, Manmatha, Pushya, ba. Amāvāsyā, Tuesday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti, corresponding to A. D. 1176, January 13, Tuesday. The saṁkrānti did not, however, occur on that day. The inscription states that Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Siṁgidēvarasa of Eḷamēlu, belonging to the Silāhāra family, Kasapayya-nāyaka, Mahāpradhāna, Daṇḍanāyaka Kumāra Bammidēvarasa, śrīkaraṇa Chākaṇayya-nāyaka, the mahāprabhu of Kummasi, Guṇḍarasa and his brother Mahādēvarasa made a gift of land and certain taxes for the worship and offerings to the temple of Svayambhū Sōmanātha. The gift was entrusted to āchārya Sōvarāsidēva. The king is stated to have been ruling from Maṅgaḷivēḍa.

cells.location: TUṄGAL, JAMKHANDI TALUK, BIJAPUR DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab near the Paramānanda temple outside the village
cells.dynasty: Sōvidēva · Sōvidēva
cells.remarks: —(Date lost) The record is badly damaged and the date-portion is lost, except the week-day, which was Thursday. Towards the end is contained another date which also is partially preserved, viz., the 5th year, Khara, eclipse. The regnal year is apparently of the same king. The inscription seems to record a gift of land for the benefit of a temple (name lost) by Mahāpradhāna Chiddarasa, Mahāprabhu Chauḍapa-Bhaṭṭōpādhyāya of agrahāra Tuṅguḷa, and others. The details of the gift are lost. It also registers a gift by a Dēvarasa and his brother (name lost) made for the benefit of the temple of Chennakēśavadēva. The king is stated to be ruling from Moḍeganūru.

cells.dynasty: Mallugi
cells.remarks: RǛGI, INDI TALUK, BIJAPUR DISTRICT Right side of a stone standing close to the front wall of the Hanumān temple Mallugi—A. D. 1176 This damaged record is dated in the second year of Mailugidēva, Durmukhi, Monday, Samkrānti; the other details are not given. It is engraved in characters of about the 12th century. During the reign-period of Mallugi, the cyclic year corres- ponded to A.D. 1176. The inscription registers a gift of land by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Chāmuṇḍarasa who was governing Taddavāḍi-1000 District, for the benefit of a temple (name lost) of the agrahāra Āneya Rūvige in Mūvattārumbāḍa. The gift was entrusted into the hands of Sarbbēśvaradēva. It also records other gifts by prabhu Brahmadēva and others (details lost).

cells.location: HIRĒ BĒVINŪR, INDI TALUK, BIJAPUR DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab set up near the temple of Bhōgaliṅga
cells.dynasty: Bhillama · Bhillama
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1190 This record is dated Śaka 1112 (nara-nētra-Śaśi-Sōma-Indu), Sādhāraṇa, Śrāvaṇa, Pūrṇimā, Thursday, corresponding to A. D. 1190, July 18. The week-day was Wednesday, when the tithi ended at 72. The inscription states that at the request of Siridēvi, the wife of Boppaṇa-nāyaka, to observe kshitiruha-nōṁpi, Daṇḍanāyaka Māyidēva, the minister of the king, planted a number of trees and established a charity fair (dharma-santhe) in Bēvinūr situated in Tardavāḍi 1000, in the presence of Mummuridaṇḍas and others of the Thirty-six-villages division. Boppaṇa-nāyaka was governing the division of Thirty-six-villages as a subordinate of Māyidēva. It also records a gift of land and house for the maintenance of the above charities made to Bandarasa, the manneya of Tarddavāḍi-1000 and to Boppaṇa- nāyaka by Māyidēva. Further gifts of trees to the temples of Taleyakāvadēva, Rēvaṇēśvara and Bhōgēśvara and also to Sōmanātha-paṇḍita, the composer of the record, are registered.

cells.remarks: —A. D. 1192 This record is dated Śaka 1115, Paridhāvi, Bhādrapada, ba. Madhyāṣṭaki, Monday, Kanyā-saṁkramaṇa. The Śaka year given was current. The details correspond to A. D. 1192, August 31, Monday, f.d.t., .14. There was no saṁkramaṇa on that day. The inscription registers the grant of the village Imguṇige, at the request of Bammeya-nāyaka, for the worship and offerings to god Kalidēva at Hipparage by the king in conjunction with Phēyiya-sāhaṇi and Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Goṇarasa of the Seḷara (Silāhāra) family and others to Rājagurudēva of Bhujagāvaḷi-kula while sarvādhikāri Malleya-Sāhaṇi was governing Tardavāḍi-nāḍu. Also records other gifts to the same god by Māyidēva-daṇḍanāyaka, the officer in charge of taxes, and by Brahmadēva-daṇḍanāyaka headed by Dēvaparasa, the prabhu of Hipparige and Pārisadēva.

cells.remarks: — A. D. 1215 This damaged and worn out record is dated in the cyclic year Yuva, Āshāḍha, Amāvāsyā, Monday, Pushya-nakshatra. In the reign of Singhaṇa, Yuva fell in A. D. 1215 and in that year the tithi corresponded to June 28 which was a Sunday and not Monday. Pushya-nakshatra coincided with the latter day. The inscription records a gift of oil for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple of god [Kēdāra]dēva, by the oil men of Purikaranagara. It appears that Māyi-paṇḍita was administering Purikaranagara at the time as a subordinate of the king. The writer of the inscription was a son of Rudrabhaṭṭōpādhyāya.

cells.remarks: — A.D. 1217 This record is dated in the king's regnal year 7, īśvara, Śrāvaṇa, Amāvāsyā, Thursday, Solar eclipse, corresponding to A.D. 1217, August 3, Thursday, f. d. t. 14. The eclipse occurred on the following day, i.e. Friday. The inscription contains a praise of the Twelve (mahājanas) and the Fifty Families of oil-men (Telligar-Aivattokkalu) of Guḷigere and registers a gift of oil for burning a perpetual lamp to the temple of Kāḷēśvara. The gift was entrusted to Tējōnidhidēva, the āchārya of the temple.

The inscription records a gift of land and house-site, after purchase from Goggiyāchārya (?), by Mūrujāvidēva, disciple of Kēdāradēva for the śrīkārya of the gods Kēdāradēva and Chikkēśvaradēva at Purikara-nagara and for the feeding of the ascetics, when Malliseṭṭi was governing the Karṇāṭa-vishaya. It also records a gift, made after purchase from Tikiseṭṭi, son of Bharatisetṭi, by the same Mūrujā- vidēva to Jñānasōma-paṇḍita, the āchārya of the Sōmanāthadēva temple for the śrīkārya of god Kēdārēśvara.

cells.location: KUNDGŌL, KUNDGOL TALUK, DHARWAR DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab in front of the Durgā temple
cells.dynasty: Singhaṇa · Siṅghaṇa
cells.remarks: — A.D. 1240 This record is dated in the king's regnal year 32, Śarvari, Chaitra, ba. 11, Wednesday, corresponding to A.D. 1240, March 20, which was a Tuesday and not Wednesday. The tithi ended on that day at .92. The inscription is in two parts. The first part, in Sanskrit language, records the gift of six nivartanas of land for the benefit of the temple of Durgā at Kundamguḷa by Mallasarma, son of Basavaṇa and grandson of Mādhavārya, with the consent of the king's minister Vāsudēva. The record was composed by Vaijanātha. The latter part of the inscription, written in Kannada language, apparently refers to the same gift mentioned above. The donor is called here Taliyara Mallayya. It also records a gift of oil made by the Fifty-Families (Aivattokkalu) of Kuindungola, for burning a perpetual lamp in the same temple. The Thousand Mahājanas of Kuindungula were to protect the gifts.

cells.location: BHATGUNKI, INDI TALUK, BIJAPUR DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab built into the pial in front of the Hanumān temple
cells.dynasty: Singhaṇa · Siṅghaṇa
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1240 This damaged record is dated in the year Śarvari, Jyeṣṭha śu. Monday, Solar eclipse. The Śaka year is lost except the last digit which is 2. Śarvari corresponds with Śaka 1162 but the existing details are irregular. The paksha given, viz., Śuddha is apparently wrong because of the mention of the solar eclipse. Again, in the month of Jyeṣṭha of the given year there was no eclipse at all. In the previous month however, i. e. Nija-Vais'ākha, both the lunar and solar eclipses occurred on Monday, the 7th and Wednesday, the 23rd respectively in May, A.D. 1240. The intended date seems to be A. D. 1240, May 23. The inscription mentions Mahāpradhāna, Sēnādhipati Bommeyanāyaka.

cells.location: KALKĒRI, SINDGI TALUK, BIJAPUR DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab in the temple called Mallayyana Guḍi
cells.dynasty: Singhaṇa · Siṅghaṇa
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1244 This record is dated Śaka 1167, Krōdhi, Bhādrapada, śu. 14, Sunday. The date is irregular. Taking the Śaka year to be current (Krōdhi), the tithi corresponds to 1244 A. D., August 18. The week day was Thursday and not Sunday as stated in the record. This long inscription gives the genealogy of Singhaṇa and records gifts of lands and house-site by pradhāni Malla, Bichaṇa and his son Pāyiseṭṭi, for the benefit of the temple of Ananta-Tirthakara at Kalukere in Hagariṭage-nāḍu constructed by Pāyi- seṭṭi, at the instance of his guru Kamalaśēna-bhaṭṭāraka. Pāyiseṭṭi, who is stated to be the son of Nākiseṭṭi, was given in adoption to Bichaṇa. Hagariṭage-nāḍu, Kalukere, Bichaṇa and his exploits, Pāyiseṭṭi and his brothers are all described at length.

cells.remarks: —A.D. 1207 This record is dated in the king's regnal year 17, Prabhava, Mārgaśira, śu. 11 Monday. The details of the date are irregular. The year Prabhava coincides with A.D. 1207, but the details do not agree with that year. But in the previous year, i.e. Kshaya, the details regularly correspond to A.D. 1206, November 13, Monday, .06, which seems to be the intended date. According to this reckoning, the commencement of his reign would be A.D. 1190-91, one year earlier than the date suggested by Fleet (Bom. Gaz., Vol. I, Pt. II, p. 503). The inscription records a gift of land for the offerings to god Svayambhū Sōmanāthadēva and for the feeding of ascetics, by Hariyama-seṭṭi, the nāḷprabhu of Kalukere, in the presence of the Mummuridaṇḍas, Kācheya-sāhaṇi and Amiteya- sāhaṇi. The gift was entrusted to Mūrujāvidēva. Supplementary gifts for the benefit of the same temple on Śivarātri and other occasions, are also recorded.

cells.remarks: —A.D. 1369 (?) This record is dated Śaka 1290, Kīlaka, Vaiśākha, ba. 30, Monday, Solar eclipse. The date is irregular. The grant was entrusted to Bikki- dēva-oḍeya, the son of Lākuḷēśvaradēva-oḍeya. The latter is described as Kadamba- rāya-kul-āchārya. The king is stated to be ruling from Hastināvatipura.

cells.remarks: —A.D. 1368 This record is dated Śaka 1290, Kīlaka, Āshāḍha śu. 1, Sunday. The date is irregular. The tithi corresponds to A.D. 1368, June 16, which was a Friday. The inscription states that when Bukkarāya's subordinate Mādhavāṅka was governing Banavāsi 12000, the latter's servant Aubhaḷanātha (i. e. Ahōbalanātha) effected repairs to the temple of Gōpinātha, in order to fulfil the desire of his master. Ahōbalanātha also requested the gauḍas and the subjects (praje) of eighteen kampanas of Gutti whereupon the latter assembling at Banavāsi, made a gift of land for the benefit of the temple, and entrusted the gift to Bikkidēva, the son (i. e. the disciple) of Lākuḷīśvaradēva. The king is stated to be ruling from Hastināvati.

cells.remarks: LAKSHMĒSVAR, SHIRHATTI TALUK, DHARWAR DISTRICT Three sides of a pillar in Sankhabasti in Rasti-baṇa Dēvarāya I—A.D. 1412 This damaged record is dated Śaka 1334, Nandana, Mārgaśira, śu. 2, Sunday, corres- ponding to A.D. 1412, November 2, Sunday. This refers to a dispute between Hēmadēvāchārya of Śankhabasti at Huligere and Sivarāmayya, the achārya of Sōmadēva temple of the same place regarding the land belonging to the respective temples. The dispute was referred to Mahāpradhāna Nāgaṇṇa-daṇḍanāyaka, at whose command purōhita Sangamadēva and the learned people of the place studied the documents (śāsana) of both the parties, and settled it in favour of Hēmadēvāchārya.

cells.remarks: There are two dates in this record. The first is dated Śaka 970, Sarvadhāri, Puṣya, ba. 7, Sunday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṃkrānti. The details given are irregular. The said tithi occurred on A.D. 1048, December 30, Friday when there was no saṃkrānti. In the previous year Sarvajit, the tithi corresponded to A.D. 1048, January 10. But there was no saṃkrānti on that day. The second date is Śaka 1009, Prabhava, Śrāvaṇa, Amāvāsyā, Sunday, solar eclipse, regularly corresponding to 1087 A.D., August 1. The inscription records the renewal of a former gift of land, which had lapsed, by the Raṭṭa Chief Kārtavīrya in conjunction with his wife Bhāgaladēvi to Jñāna- śakti-vratīndra, disciple of Sōmēśvara-paṇḍitadēva of Puliyarasara-maṭha. It is 1 This inscription is noticed in JBBRAS, Vol. X, pp. 172-73. stated that the former gift was made by Mahāsāmanta Aṅkarasa, grandfather (actually grandfather's brother) of Kārtavīrya, to Sōmēśvara-Paṇḍitadēva for the benefit of the temple of Ankēśvara built by him at Sugandhavarti. It is also stated that Aṅkarasa was a feudatory of Trailōkyamalla (Sōmēśvara I). The record is damaged and worn out.

cells.dynasty: Vikrama (?) · Vikrama
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1081 This inscription is dated in the 12th regnal year of Kādamba Chakravarti Vīra- [ma], Durmati, Kārtika ba. 5, Monday. This Vīra[ma] may be a mistake for Vikrama. In that case Vikrama will have to be identified with the son of Jayasiṁha. It may be noted however that no inscription of this Vikrama has as yet been found and it is doubtful if he ruled at all. The details of the date may be equated with A.D. 1081, October 25, Monday. It may also be noted that Kīrtidēva who came after him has for him a date as early as 1068 A.D. It records the death, by the rite of samādhi, of Bhōgave, the wife of Tippiseṭṭi Sātaya. She is stated to be the lay disciple of Sakalachandra-bhaṭṭāraka belonging to Dēsi-gaṇa, Pustaka-gachchha, and Koṇḍakuṇd-ānvaya

cells.remarks: BĀḶAMBĪḌ, HANGAL TALUK, DHARWAR DISTRICT Hero stone set up in the temple of Rāmēśvara Tailapa The inscription which refers itself to Tailahadēva ruling from Naraymagal is dated in the 2nd year of his reign, Prajāpati, Kārtika, śu. Pūrṇimā, Monday. The name Tailaha suggests that he belonged to the family of the Kadambas of Hāngal. But the 2nd year of none of the Tailahas of this family coincided with the cyclic year Prajāpati. It records a grant of land at Kalkere made by Bammagauḍa, in honour of his father who died in a raid made by Tailaha on Baḷḷarabīḍu in course of his attack on Huriṭigi-nāḍu, the fort of which was in charge of a certain Sōvarasa. </content>

cells.remarks: JAMKHANDI JAMKHANDI TALUK, BIJAPUR DISTRICT Broken slab from Olyappa's Maṭha now kept in the house of Mr. W.T. Apte A.D. 1082 This record is dated in the cyclic year [Dundubhi], Chaitra, ba. 5, Monday, Viśuva-saṁkrānti, Solar eclipse. Obviously the eclipse could not have occurred on the given tithi. On grounds of palæography the date may be equated with A.D. 1082 March 21, Monday. The saṁkrānti did not occur on that day. It registers a gift of land to god Uttarēśvara of Jambukhaṇḍi. The beginning of the record is lost.

cells.remarks: D. 1168 The available details of the date in this damaged record are Śaka 1090, and Āsvayuja, Paurṇamāsi, Thursday, lunar eclipse. The date corresponds to A. D. 1168, September 19, Thursday if the Śaka year is 1090 itself. The eclipse occurred on the previous day when the tithi commenced after .04. It also registers a gift of land and income from taxes to god Svayambhudēva, by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Chauṇḍarasa of the Silāhāra family on the occasion of a lunar eclipse.

cells.remarks: This record is dated Śaka 1115 (given in words), Virōdhikṛit, Uttarāyaṇa. The cyclic year given corresponds to Śaka 1113 and not 1115. The inscription registers a gift of land by the One Thousand of the mahāgrahāra (name lost) for a well caused to be constructed by Ermmeyara Māḍiyaṇa. cells.remarks: 12th Century A.D. This record is dated the cyclic year Sādhāraṇa, Tadige, Friday. The details of the date cannot be verified. cells.place: Slab lying in Hirēmatha.
cells.dynasty: Miscellaneous
cells.remarks: D. 1609] The extant portion of the date of this damaged record is Saumya, Pushya, śu. 13, Wednesday, Uttarāyaṇa-samkramaṇa. On palaeographical grounds the date may be probably equated with A.D. 1609, December 27, Wednesday, f.d.t. 66. The _saṁkra- maṇa_ occurred on the next day. The inscription registers a gift of oil for a lamp to a deity by some trade-guilds (_sameya_) at Kalkere.

cells.remarks: D. 1714 This record is dated Śaka 1635, Jaya, Mārgaśira, śu. Champā-shashṭhi, correspond- ing to A. D. 1714, December 1, the Śaka year being 1636. cells.location: KĀMADHĒNU, KALGHATGI TALUK, DHARWAR DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab lying in front of the Kalleśvara temple
cells.dynasty: Bhūlōkamalla (Sōmēśvara III) · Sōmēśvara III
cells.remarks: —A. D. 1129 This record is dated Chālukya-Vikrama year 54, Saumya, Chaitra śu. 2, Monday, Saṁkrānti. The tithi corresponds to A. D. 1129, March 23 which was Saturday. The Mēsha-saṁkrānti occurred on the next day. The inscription records a gift of land and money to god Kalidēvasvāmi of Sāsalu by Malliseṭṭi of Hulivara when Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Jayakēsidēva of the Kadamba family was governing Koṁkaṇa-900 and Palasige-12000 divisions. The gift land which was purchased by the donor from Sōmēśvara-bhaṭṭa, the son of Nārāyaṇa- bhaṭṭa, the ūroḍeya of Sāsalu, and two others, was entrusted into the hands of Tējōrāśi-paṇḍita, the disciple of Dēvarāśi-paṇḍita, the āchārya of the temple. The record gives a genealogical account of the donor.
